title: Choosing a Debate Motion
text:
Every debate begins with a motion, which is a statement that the teams must argue for or against. A good motion is clear and balanced, so that both sides have strong arguments. Organizers often publish the motion a week in advance. This gives teams time to research the topic.

Teams usually divide their work carefully. The first speaker introduces the case, while the second speaker answers the other team's main points. Many coaches say that the most important part is the final summary, because it reminds the judges why the team should win.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, when do organizers often publish the motion?
options: On the day of the debate

questions.text: What does the first speaker do, according to the second paragraph?
Why is a clear and balanced motion useful for a debate?
options: It lets both sides have strong arguments
It removes the need for any research
It ensures that one team always wins
It makes the final summary unnecessary

questions.text: What can be inferred about the final summary?
options: It can influence how the judges decide
It is usually the shortest part of a debate
It is given before the motion is announced
It is meant only for the audience

vocabulary.definition: a statement that teams must argue for or against
fair, giving equal weight to both sides
to study a topic in detail to find information
a short statement of the main points

paragraph_translations: Кожні дебати починаються з теми, тобто твердження, за або проти якого команди мають аргументувати. Хороша тема є чіткою і збалансованою, щоб обидві сторони мали сильні аргументи. Організатори часто оприлюднюють тему за тиждень наперед. Це дає командам час вивчити це питання.

Команди зазвичай ретельно розподіляють роботу. Перший промовець представляє позицію, а другий відповідає на головні тези іншої команди. Багато тренерів кажуть, що найважливіша частина — це заключний підсумок, адже він нагадує суддям, чому команда має перемогти.
